Your body uses light to help figure out what time it is. What are you telling it at 10 p.m.?

When we wrote Deskbound, one of the things we wanted people to think about was how the modern environment can shape physiology without us paying much attention to it.

Light is a great example.

Your circadian system uses light exposure as an important time cue, and the light you encounter in the evening can influence melatonin production and sleep timing. 

So if your house is lit up like a Costco and you’re staring into bright screens right up until bed, that’s worth examining.

Did we stop gathering and then stop drinking? Or are we gathering less because we aren’t drinking?

It’s true that fewer adults under 35 drink alcohol. But the alarming stat is that the time Americans spend at social gatherings has dropped by half in two decades.

And that matters. Social isolation carries a mortality risk akin to smoking.

But the answer to isolation isn’t necessarily more alcohol. It’s more invitations.
